findings.finding:
The round-3 reading still differs from how systemd v256 reads /proc/cmdline, in two ways.
(1) Single quotes. proc_cmdline_strv_internal (src/basic/proc-cmdline.c) splits the line with EXTRACT_UNQUOTE|EXTRACT_RELAX|EXTRACT_RETAIN_ESCAPE. In extract_first_word (src/basic/extract-word.c), EXTRACT_UNQUOTE treats both ' and " as quote characters, anywhere in a word, and removes them. The schema refuses only ", so the README sentence 'A command line may not contain ", so splitting on spaces gives the words the kernel and systemd see' holds for the kernel but not for systemd.
- Probe N1: ENROLLED is the positive's line plus " systemd.unit='planeon-maintenance.target'". With every capture rebound, check_qualification ACCEPTS it. systemd unquotes the word to systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target and boots the maintenance target.
- N2 ("'systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target'") and N3 ("systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance''.target") are also ACCEPTED.
- N5: a MAINTENANCE line followed by " 'systemd.unit=multi-user.target'" is ACCEPTED, but systemd boots multi-user.target.
(2) Runlevel words. parse_proc_cmdline_item (src/core/main.c) also sets arg_default_unit from any bare word that runlevel_to_target (src/basic/unit-file.c, rlmap) maps to a target: emergency and -b to emergency.target; rescue, single, -s, s, S and 1 to rescue.target; 2, 3 and 4 to multi-user.target; 5 to graphical.target. These words and systemd.unit= share last-wins. The README's 'the last systemd.unit= wins' is therefore incomplete.
- N6, N7 and N8: a MAINTENANCE line followed by ' 3', ' rescue' or ' -- emergency' is ACCEPTED, but systemd boots multi-user, rescue or emergency.
The kernel side is correct. next_arg (lib/cmdline.c) treats only " specially, so the lockdown test (words before the first bare '--') agrees with parse_args. N11 (lockdown='integrity'), N12 (a leading '--') and V49 are refused. N13 (lockdown=none after lockdown=integrity) is accepted, which matches lockdown_param, since the level can only be raised.
The K1 discriminator itself is not affected: distinct entry IDs and command lines, with every capture bound to the enrolled line's hash. Like R2-1, this is an analysis error on observed data in the token rules. It defeats their stated purpose: the enrolled entry never names the maintenance target, and the maintenance entry selects it.
findings.requiredChange:
- Refuse ' in kernelCmdline as well, for example with the pattern ^[ !#-&(-~]+$. A space split then equals both next_arg and systemd's EXTRACT_UNQUOTE|EXTRACT_RETAIN_ESCAPE split. Alternatively, unquote both quote characters as extract_first_word does.
- For the MAINTENANCE entry, take the effective default unit as the last of its valid systemd.unit= values and the v256 runlevel words (rlmap), and require that unit to be planeon-maintenance.target.
- Add vectors for N1 and N6, and for N5 if ' stays allowed.
- Restate the README K1 row, decision 2 and the model comment at line 243.

tree_content holds the digests of every record file under /opt/planeon/python/, not only the interpreter's runtime and modules.
Probe W4-b: SERVER lists /opt/planeon/python/3.12.14/lib/libssl.so.3, and EFFECT_GATE lists /opt/planeon/lib/libssl.so.3 with the same sha256 and verity, at its own inode. The result is 'native-only role closure lists an interpreter'.
A host that installs one OpenSSL, libffi or zlib build both in the Python tree and in the native library directory is plausible and legitimate. The README's 'by path or by content' wording covers the case, but the row describes the tree as 'its runtime library and modules', which reads narrower. This is not a security weakness.

questionAnswers.Q0:
The round-3 bytes make the README dispositions true for R2-2 to R2-7 and for W9.
R2-1, and with it W6, is PARTIAL. The double-quote, after-'--' and last-systemd.unit= cases are fixed and pinned (V52-V54, A08), and W6-a, W6-b, W6-c, W6-d and W6-e now give the systemd-correct result. But systemd's EXTRACT_UNQUOTE also removes single quotes, and runlevel words take part in the default-unit last-wins (R3-1). The README sentences claiming the space split equals what 'the kernel and systemd see' and 'the last systemd.unit= wins' are therefore inaccurate.
No item that earlier rounds CLOSED has reopened: W1-W5, W7, W8 and the twelve carried items.
questionAnswers.Q1: All twelve carried items are CLOSED as required: P1, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7(a), P7(b), P7(c), the network-policy agent identity, the W02e label slots, E1's census and K1. Round 3 changed only the boot-entry rules, the native-only content rule, the inode rule's messages and the descendant-count message. The schema diff from round 2 is only the two kernelCmdline patterns.
questionAnswers.Q3:
All four facts hold in Linux v6.12, and the four README digests match the files fetched at tag v6.12.
- Attach types: the 22 census types plus the 7 hooks are exactly to_cgroup_bpf_attach_type's 28 types plus BPF_LSM_CGROUP, which is the set of uapi bpf_attach_type names containing CGROUP.
- Effective query: __cgroup_bpf_query with BPF_F_QUERY_EFFECTIVE copies cgrp->bpf.effective[atype], advancing prog_ids for each atype. For BPF_LSM_CGROUP it spans CGROUP_LSM_START..CGROUP_LSM_END (10 slots with CONFIG_BPF_LSM). compute_effective_progs adds ancestor programs when the ancestor has BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI, or when no nearer program exists.
- pids.current: pids_can_fork charges 1 per copy_process, and pids_release uncharges, so it counts tasks.
- /proc/<pid>/exe: exec_binprm swaps bprm->file for bprm->interpreter, begin_new_exec calls set_mm_exe_file, and proc_exe_link returns the exe file's path. The link therefore names the interpreter.
The command-line facts behind R3-1 come from the same reads: next_arg handles only ", and parse_args stops at a bare '--'. systemd v256 is cited in R3-1.

reviewLimit:
This is a source-level, DATA_CHECK_ONLY review of the five subject files at commit 48b20dc (tree 4fa1b2d3). The files were hash-verified at the start and end of the review.
It establishes no native qualification. It establishes no kernel, SELinux, cgroup, BPF, boot-loader, systemd or TPM behaviour, no installed profile, selected distribution or seccomp filter, and no E01-E12 obligation. It authorizes nothing.
The kernel and systemd facts come from reading the Linux v6.12 and systemd v256 sources, not from running them.
Repository tests and validators were not run. The v3 model was imported read-only from byte-identical copies and executed only through my own scripts in /private/tmp/claude-501/w02af-review3/. The v2 model was diffed, not executed.
The out-of-subject working-tree edits were not reviewed. Only the repository, my scratch directory and public source URLs were accessed. No GitHub, runner, sudo, cloud, native or warm-source action was taken.
